item.title: JPMorgan in Talks for $3.8B Construction Loan for 80 West 67th Street Supertall
item.description: JPMorgan is in talks for a $3.8 billion construction loan for a luxury supertall condominium project on Manhattan's Upper West Side.
item.content:encoded:
JPMorgan Chase is in talks with developer Extell Development for a $3.8 billion construction loan to build one of Manhattan's tallest luxury condominium projects at 80 West 67th Street on the Upper West Side, according to a Bloomberg report citing anonymous sources. The financing, if completed, would rank among the largest construction loans ever arranged in the United States. Both companies declined to comment.
Project Details and Location
The proposed tower would replace part of the former Walt Disney Co. and ABC headquarters campus. New York City Department of Buildings filings describe a roughly 1.2 million-square-foot supertall rising 86 stories, with 430 residential units, about 25,000 square feet of retail, and parking. At nearly 1,200 feet, it would stand more than 400 feet above the neighborhood's next-tallest building, which was also developed by Extell.
Extell, led by Gary Barnett, assembled the parcels in early 2022 for roughly $930 million. The site spans about 1.7 million square feet of development rights across West 66th and 67th streets. The project has already drawn pushback from some neighbors over its height and the absence of affordable units, even though Barnett has offered concessions and could legally build a 1,500-foot tower with no affordability requirement under current zoning.
This Upper West Side scheme is part of a larger package backed by an undisclosed preferred equity partner contributing $1.2 billion, first reported by Bisnow last year. The package also includes The Torch, a Times Square hotel development that recently secured nearly $1.3 billion in financing and has been built past 40 stories.
Financing Structure and Risk
The reported loan amount is extraordinary for a single construction facility. Lenders generally size construction debt against total development cost, projected sellout, and presales; a $3.8 billion facility on a project expected to yield 430 condominiums implies very high per-unit values. The project's Upper West Side location, rather than Billionaires' Row on West 57th Street, means absorption and pricing assumptions will be closely scrutinized by credit committees.
The presence of a $1.2 billion preferred equity partner across the wider Extell package is one factor that could reduce JPMorgan's effective risk by placing substantial junior capital beneath the senior loan. This is not simply a real estate bet; it is a financing structure that relies on trophy pricing, patient equity, and a lender willing to underwrite supertall execution risk at a scale rarely seen outside office towers.
The project has already generated protests over height and affordability, yet Extell's position is unusually strong. Because existing zoning would permit a taller building with no affordable units, the concessions Barnett has offered should be read as negotiation from strength rather than regulatory necessity. That reduces the near-term risk that community pressure will shrink the project below its planned 1.2 million square feet, though it does not eliminate design, permit, and public-approval friction.
Implications for JPMorgan and the Market
For JPMorgan, the Upper West Side loan would sit alongside broader exposure to Barnett's pipeline. The project is one portion of a package that includes The Torch hotel near Times Square, where a separate nearly $1.3 billion financing recently closed. The practical effect is that JPMorgan and the unnamed equity partner are evaluating a multi-asset relationship, not an isolated transaction, which can support more aggressive terms on any single asset but also links the lender's performance to execution across several complex construction projects.
If the loan closes, it would signal that at least one major U.S. bank is willing to commit historically large construction capital to ultra-luxury condominiums despite elevated interest rates and construction costs. It would also test whether buyers accept Billionaires' Row-style pricing north of Lincoln Square. The scale is a single data point, but an important one: it suggests top-tier lenders still see deep demand for scarce, high-floor Manhattan condominium inventory.
For real estate and finance professionals, the next concrete signal is whether JPMorgan and Extell move from reported talks to a signed credit agreement, at which point loan sizing, covenants, and presale requirements would become visible. Until then, the terms remain unconfirmed.
Track the New York City Department of Buildings file for 80 West 67th Street to see whether the 1.2 million-square-foot, 86-story plan changes after neighborhood concessions; a final unit count and square footage are the clearest indicators of whether Extell is buying certainty or maximizing envelope. Treat the reported $3.8 billion figure with caution until a signed agreement is disclosed.

item.title: Ireland press conference before Israel games delayed as pressure to boycott grows
item.description: Ireland's national football team is experiencing internal conflict and external pressure regarding their upcoming games against Israel.
item.content:encoded:
Pressure to boycott upcoming Nations League games against Israel over that country's actions in Gaza took its toll on the Ireland team Saturday when players talked for hours, voted on their participation, and one departed the squad.
Ireland is due to play Israel in Debrecen, Hungary in the first of those games Sunday, but the team’s press conference and training session Saturday were delayed by more than five hours as the players again held discussions among themselves in the team hotel over whether they should play.
Bazunu takes a stand
Gavin Bazunu later confirmed on social media that he had left the squad. He said he felt it would be "wrong to participate" in the games "based purely upon my personal belief that the killing of innocent people is wrong."
The 24-year-old reserve goalkeeper stressed his stance was “not in opposition of the Israeli people or the Jewish community but against the atrocities in the region. There are few times where you get a chance in life to stand up for something bigger and I strongly believe that this is one of them.”
David Courell, the CEO of the Football Association of Ireland, said at a long-delayed press conference earlier that an unnamed player's “discomfort with fulfilling this fixture” had caused deliberations for the rest of the squad. He said a vote was taken among the players and that “a significant majority” favored continuing with the games.
“Based on that, the association took the decision on behalf of Irish football that this fixture would continue as we have always intended to fulfill the fixtures,” Courell said.
Bazunu, who reportedly told the team Friday night that he did not want to play, was not mentioned in the press conference, but Ireland coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said a player was leaving.
“All the rest of the players are training today,” Hallgrimsson said. “It’s an ongoing discussion and we haven’t come to a kind of conclusion on this, but we are going ahead, the game is going ahead, we’re going to train. And there will be more discussions tonight and probably tomorrow."
Black armbands
Courell said the players were uncomfortable dealing with questions “that are not about football” so they had requested not to have to deal with media obligations around Sunday's match.
“They also have the intention of wearing black armbands in recognition of all lives lost in the conflict," Courell said. "And also there will be elements of the pre-match ceremony that will not be partaken in.”
He added that both the players and the FAI will be making a “significant contribution” to charity from both match fees – neither of which is open to Irish fans – and from Ireland's game against Austria in Dublin on Oct. 1.
Ireland's national broadcaster RTÉ said last week it will only provide stripped-back coverage of the games vs. Israel to meet contractual obligations — with no studio presentation, commentary on the international feed, or analysis — while it will also not accept advertising or sponsorship around either game.
RTÉ also announced last week that Ireland will boycott the Eurovision Song Contest for a second year over Israel's participation.
Pressure builds
The Ireland team has been coming under increasing pressure at home, where affinity with Palestinians is strong, to boycott the two games against Israel — Israel's “home” game Sunday and Ireland’s “home” game in Backa Topola, Serbia on Oct. 4.
The FAI said in June that Ireland's home game was moving to a neutral venue for "operational reasons" and that no fans will be present. That followed widespread calls to boycott the match, and the FAI's own motion the previous November calling on UEFA to ban Israel from club and international competitions.
“There’s a huge support – probably in Europe the biggest support – for Palestine in Ireland,” Hallgrimsson said. “And there’s been protests since the draw (in February) not to play this fixture. There’s been a protest from day one not to play the fixture in Ireland and that’s the pressure that the players will feel and the association will feel. I felt that pressure growing day by day and it’s getting almost to a breaking limit now.”
Ireland midfielder Jason Knight said after Thursday’s 1-0 loss in Kosovo that the players were in a difficult situation and that he didn’t think the matches should be going ahead.
Hallgrimsson previously said "we're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide. We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel" — drawing a furious reaction from the Israeli soccer federation, which accused the Icelandic coach of "stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy."
The FAI had resisted calls to boycott the matches, arguing the team could be hit with punishing sanctions by UEFA. Ireland is co-hosting the 2028 European Championship with England, Wales and Scotland.
More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter urging the FAI to reconsider its decision to go ahead with the fixtures.
There were protesters outside the team hotel in Dublin last week calling on the players to boycott the games. The SIPTU trade union displayed a huge poster in central Dublin beside the River Liffey asking the players to “Go with your conscience!” and “Don't play with genocide” beside an image of a blood-splattered ball.
Former Ireland coach Brian Kerr said the FAI had “lost the respect of the Irish people” for going ahead with the games.
“The Irish people and the soccer-going public don’t want the games to be played,” Kerr said. “I think they’ve made their opinions clear over the last year. The FAI back in November actually went to UEFA and requested that Israel be put out of the tournament on a principle. And yet they went against that principle.”
UEFA did not respond to a request for comment on Saturday's developments.

item.title: Smart løsning: Danskerne betaler gæld for 1,2 mia.
item.description: A new digital solution in Denmark has helped citizens and businesses pay 1.2 billion DKK in public debt since its 2024 launch.
item.content:encoded:
Danskere og virksomheder har betalt gæld til det offentlige for 1,2 milliarder kroner gennem Gældsstyrelsens digitale løsning 'Mit gældsoverblik'.
Det oplyser Gældsstyrelsen i en pressemeddelelse. Siden lanceringen i 2024 har omkring 172.000 borgere og 3.000 virksomheder betalt via løsningen.
Alene i årets første otte måneder er omkring 56.000 skyldnere blevet gældfri efter en indbetaling på 'Mit gældsoverblik', oplyser styrelsen.
Vil du gerne være økonomisk fri, er det faktisk relativt simpelt. Du kan prøve Ekstra Bladets beregner her.
Betaler med mobilenFor syv ud af ti, der har foretaget en indbetaling, er valget faldet på MobilePay. Resten har især brugt betalingskort.
- Det er jo fantastisk at se, at vi har fået indbetalinger for langt over en milliard kr. ved at gøre det nemt og tilgængeligt at komme af med sin gæld med et klik, udtaler skatte- og vækstminister Jakob Engel-Schmidt i pressemeddelelsen, inden han tilføjer:
- Det viser, hvor vigtigt det er, at vi har et system, der gør det nemt for borgerne – og at alle har let adgang til oplysninger om deres gæld, så de kan betale den.
Han peger på, at borgerne skal have let adgang til oplysninger om deres gæld, hvis de skal kunne betale den.
'Mit gældsoverblik' er blevet besøgt over to millioner gange siden lanceringen. Her kan skyldnere se deres gæld til det offentlige og betale med kort eller MobilePay.
I hele 2025 blev omkring 34.000 skyldnere ifølge styrelsens nye opgørelse gældfri efter en indbetaling via løsningen.

item.title: Chile AFP Pension Surplus Withdrawals Rise to US$58 Million in First Half of 2026
item.description: Chilean pensioners withdrew US$58 million in surplus funds in the first half of 2026, with an average of CLP 17.9 million per withdrawal.
item.content:encoded:
Chilean pensioners withdrew US$58 million in surplus funds from their AFP accounts in the first half of 2026, with an average of CLP 17.9 million per withdrawal, new data show.
Chilean pensioners withdrew US$58 million in surplus funds from their individual pension system during the first half of 2026, with 3,138 withdrawals at an average of CLP 17.9 million each, according to a report from the Asociación de AFP. The surplus, known as the excedente, is the freely available balance remaining after a retiree finances a required pension. The figure compares with US$58 million in withdrawals and an average of CLP 16.7 million per withdrawal in the same period of 2025.
The benefit allows a person who is already retired to withdraw part or all of their accumulated balance after financing the pension required by law. The data cover the period from January to June 2026.
Chile AFP Surplus Withdrawals Under Eligibility Rules
To qualify through the standard route, a member must have at least 10 years of affiliation, be receiving a pension equal to at least 70 percent of their average income during the ten years before retirement, and have a pension above UF 12, an inflation-indexed unit used in Chile.
The AFP association reported 3,138 withdrawals in the first half of 2026, with an average of CLP 17.9 million per withdrawal. The year-earlier period saw the same dollar total of US$58 million, but a lower average of CLP 16.7 million.
Although the first-half total rose year on year, the long-term picture is one of decline. Since 2004, roughly 262,000 pensioners have used the mechanism, withdrawing about US$3.05 billion in total.
Annual withdrawals fell from almost 21,000 in 2004 to a low of 5,859 in 2025, and have remained below 10,000 since 2020.
Decline in Pension Surplus Withdrawals Since 2020
The AFP association attributes the decline to extraordinary pension withdrawals that reduced many members' balances and therefore their ability to generate surplus at retirement. That is the association's interpretation of the data, not a directly measured causal effect in the report.
The pattern is consistent with that explanation: withdrawals collapsed after 2020, just as the extraordinary withdrawal episodes reduced balances across the system, and the full-year 2025 figure was the lowest on record.
The profile of users has also changed substantially. Since Law 19.934 took effect in 2004, the criteria for early retirement have become stricter.
The pension a member must finance rose gradually from at least 50 percent of average taxable wages and 110 percent of the minimum old-age pension to 70 percent and 150 percent.
As a result, early-retirement withdrawals fell from 16,701 in 2004 to 2,793 in 2025, and their share of all withdrawals dropped from 80.8 percent to 47.7 percent.
In the first half of 2026, early retirement represented 42.2 percent of withdrawals, old-age retirement 38.3 percent and disability 19.5 percent.
Terminal Illness Route Under Law 21.309
A separate terminal-illness route was created by Law 21.309 in 2021. People with a life expectancy of 12 months or less can access funds early through a temporary income calculated for their estimated remaining life, while protecting resources needed for survivors.
From January to May 2026, this route recorded US$14.3 million in withdrawals, with an average of CLP 33.9 million per person, well above the overall average.
The terminal-illness option is producing much larger individual withdrawals than the standard route. That likely reflects the design of the benefit, which allows the temporary pension to be reduced to the level of the Basic Solidarity Pension for people over 80 and the remaining balance to be withdrawn as surplus.
More than 4,400 people have used this channel since the law came into force, withdrawing about US$143 million.
What Pensioners Should Check Before Withdrawing
For Chilean pensioners and affiliates considering this benefit, the rules and trends point to several concrete checks. First, confirm the standard eligibility threshold: at least 10 years of affiliation, a pension equal to or above 70 percent of average income in the ten years before retirement, and a pension above UF 12.
Second, if you have a life expectancy of 12 months or less, ask your AFP about the terminal-illness route under Law 21.309. It permits earlier access and the option to reduce the temporary pension to the Basic Solidarity Pension for people over 80, withdrawing the rest as surplus.
Third, do not use historical peaks as an expectation. The average standard withdrawal was CLP 17.9 million in the first half of 2026, while terminal-illness withdrawals averaged CLP 33.9 million. Your result depends on your balance and the pension you must finance.
Fourth, if you are considering early retirement, note that the required pension threshold is now 70 percent of average taxable wages and 150 percent of the minimum old-age pension, so fewer people are generating surplus through this route than before 2005.

item.title: Swiss National Bank’s Schlegel watching hot weather impact on food price inflation
item.description: A Swiss National Bank official notes that hot weather has impacted food prices but not significantly Swiss inflation.
item.content:encoded:
ZURICH, Sept 26 (Reuters) - This year’s record temperatures have had an impact on food prices but have not been a factor behind rising Swiss inflation, Swiss National Bank Chairman Martin Schlegel said in an interview broadcast on Saturday.
Switzerland’s annual inflation rate doubled in August to its highest in nearly two years, raising concerns about smaller harvests and lower water levels on transport routes like the Danube and the Rhine making food more expensive and driving up prices overall.
The SNB is closely monitoring the impact of the hot weather on food prices, Schlegel told radio station SRF.
"The hot summer, especially the dry summer, has had an effect on food prices — you can certainly see that there have been certain price movements," Schlegel said.
"There are also policy measures taken to counteract that, and so far the rise in inflation is almost exclusively attributable to petroleum products," he added.
The SNB held its benchmark interest rate at 0% on Thursday, even as other central banks hike borrowing costs to tackle rising inflation linked to more expensive fuel.
It could do this because the SNB expects inflation to decline after a temporary increase, and remain within its 0% to 2% target to the end of its forecast range, which runs to mid-2029, Schlegel said.
"We assume that the price of crude oil will come back down, and that simply means that the effect of a higher oil price at the moment gradually fades out a little over time," he said.
Schlegel also said the recent downturn in the value of the franc was a small change after years of appreciation.
"There have been long periods when the franc actually became a bit stronger almost constantly," he said. "What we’ve just seen is a minor counter-trend."

item.title: Portable Water Filtration Systems: Flexible Water Treatment for Travel, Outdoor and Remote Use
item.description: This article discusses the factors to consider when choosing a portable water filtration system for travel, outdoor activities, or remote living.
item.content:encoded:
Access to a suitable water supply is an important consideration when travelling, spending time outdoors or staying in a property away from conventional mains services. In these situations, a portable water filtration system can provide a flexible way to treat water without relying on a permanent whole-property installation.
Portable filtration can be relevant to a wide range of situations, from camping and mobile accommodation to boats, temporary properties and remote living. However, portability should not be the only factor considered when choosing equipment. Water source, filtration technology, capacity, pressure and maintenance can all influence whether a particular system is appropriate.
Why Consider Portable Water Filtration?
Permanent water treatment systems are not practical for every situation. Someone travelling between locations, living temporarily in a mobile property or managing a remote building may need equipment that can work within changing circumstances.
Portable filtration systems can offer greater flexibility because they are not necessarily tied to one fixed plumbing installation. This can make them useful for people who move between locations or need a treatment solution for a temporary setup.
They can also be relevant when a property has limited space. A small mobile home, campervan or boat may not have room for a conventional treatment installation, making compact equipment easier to accommodate.
The important point is to match the filtration method to the water rather than choosing a system simply because it is easy to transport.
Where Might Portable Systems Be Used?
Portable water filtration has applications across several types of travel and independent living.
Outdoor enthusiasts may consider filtration when travelling away from conventional water infrastructure. Owners of motorhomes and caravans may also need to manage water differently from people living in permanent homes.
Boats and other mobile accommodation can have their own storage tanks and plumbing arrangements, creating different requirements for water treatment.
Portable filtration can also be useful for remote properties where a permanent treatment installation is impractical or where flexibility is important.
Each situation has different requirements, however. A system designed for occasional outdoor use may not be suitable for continuous domestic demand. Checking the equipment’s intended application is therefore essential.
Start With the Water Source
Before choosing a portable filter, identify where the water will come from.
A treated mains supply is different from water collected from a natural source. Rivers, streams, springs, boreholes and stored water can all have different characteristics.
Where water comes from a private or uncertain source, testing can help establish what treatment may be required. It is important not to assume that a portable filter will address every potential water-quality issue.
The filtration technology needs to be matched to the substances or particles that need to be reduced. Some systems focus primarily on sediment, while membrane-based technologies can provide a more selective filtration process.
Understanding the source is therefore the foundation of choosing suitable equipment.
How Membrane Filtration Can Help
Membrane filtration is one technology that can be incorporated into water treatment systems intended for mobile or independent applications.
A membrane acts as a selective barrier. Water is passed through the membrane under suitable conditions, while certain substances are retained according to the membrane’s characteristics.
Different membrane technologies operate at different levels of filtration. Microfiltration, ultrafiltration, nanofiltration and reverse osmosis are examples, each with different characteristics and applications.
This variety means that “membrane filter” is not a description of one universal type of equipment. The exact membrane, pressure requirements and treatment capabilities should always be checked against the intended use.
For mobile applications, the overall system also needs to work within the available space, water pressure and power arrangements.
Capacity Matters When You Are Away From Home
Portable equipment may be compact, but that does not mean every compact system has the same capacity.
Consider how much water will be required each day. Someone travelling alone for short periods will have different requirements from a family spending several weeks in a motorhome.
Peak usage is also worth considering. Drinking, cooking, washing and other activities can increase demand, depending on how the equipment is being used.
If the system has a specified flow rate, compare this with the expected demand. A system that works well for occasional use may not be appropriate for continuous high-volume requirements.
Pressure and Power Requirements
Portable water treatment equipment may require a particular level of water pressure to operate effectively.
This is especially relevant in mobile properties, where water may be supplied by a pump rather than directly from a mains connection. The pressure available from the pump should be checked against the requirements of the filtration system.
Power is another consideration. Some portable setups may operate without significant electrical requirements, while others can include pumps or additional equipment.
For people using solar panels, batteries or other independent power sources, energy consumption may need to be considered as part of the overall system design.
Storage and Transport
A portable system should also be practical to handle.
Think about where it will be stored when not in use and whether it needs protection during transport. Equipment that is moved regularly may experience more handling than a permanent household installation.
Connections and fittings should be checked for compatibility with the water supply being used. It is also sensible to understand how the system should be drained, cleaned or stored between periods of use.
Following the manufacturer’s instructions can help prevent avoidable problems when equipment is transported or placed into storage.
Maintenance While Travelling
Maintenance can be more challenging when you are away from home.
Filter cartridges may need replacement, while some membrane systems may require cleaning or other servicing. Before travelling, users should understand the expected maintenance schedule and make sure suitable replacement components are available.
This is particularly important for longer journeys or trips to remote locations where replacement parts may not be easy to obtain.
Keeping track of filter usage can also help prevent maintenance from being forgotten during a busy trip.
When Portable Filtration Is Not Enough
Portable filtration can be useful, but it should not automatically be regarded as a complete water treatment solution.
The appropriate treatment depends on the source and quality of the water. Filtration may address certain physical or dissolved substances depending on the technology, while other treatment methods are designed for different purposes.
Ultraviolet treatment, for example, uses UV-C radiation rather than a physical membrane. For people researching different treatment technologies, LED UV water treatment can be considered where ultraviolet disinfection is appropriate to the application.
In some circumstances, multiple treatment stages may be used together. The correct combination should be determined by the characteristics of the water and the requirements of the system.
Choosing the Right Portable System
When comparing portable filtration equipment, consider more than its size.
Ask what type of water it is designed to treat, what filtration technology it uses and how much water it can process. Check pressure and power requirements, particularly if the system will be installed in a motorhome, boat or remote property.
Maintenance is equally important. Find out how often filters or membranes need attention and whether replacement parts are readily available.
Finally, think about how the system will fit into everyday use. The best-designed equipment is of limited practical value if it is difficult to transport, install, operate or maintain.
Conclusion
Portable water filtration systems can provide a flexible option for people who need water treatment away from a conventional fixed installation. Their potential applications include travel, outdoor activities, mobile accommodation and remote properties.
Choosing the right system requires careful consideration of the water source, filtration technology, capacity, pressure, power and maintenance. A compact design is useful, but it should still be capable of meeting the requirements of the intended application.
By understanding the water that needs to be treated and comparing systems according to their actual specifications, travellers and remote-property owners can select a filtration approach that fits their circumstances while avoiding unrealistic expectations about what any single treatment technology can achieve.
